source_note: Compiled by the team from published literature. Demo draft — NOT medical advice. Real deployment requires pharmacist/physician review. The system flags risk only; it never changes prescriptions.

rules.label: Anticholinergics
rules.indications: Overactive bladder / urinary incontinence, allergy, Parkinson's disease
rules.patient_advice: This medicine can stop you sweating normally, so your body cools down less well. Stay somewhere cool on hot days. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)
rules.reviewed_by: UNREVIEWED — team draft, needs pharmacist/physician review

rules.label: Diuretics ("water pills")
rules.clinician_note: Monitor weight and urine output; hydrate adequately
rules.patient_advice: This medicine makes you pass more water, so you can get dehydrated faster in the heat. Keep drinking water and tell your doctor if you feel dizzy or very tired. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)
rules.reviewed_by: UNREVIEWED — team draft, needs pharmacist/physician review

rules.label: Antipsychotics
rules.clinician_note: Caregivers must be informed; ensure a cooled environment
rules.patient_advice: This medicine can make it harder for your body to control its temperature. Stay in a cool place on hot days. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)
rules.reviewed_by: UNREVIEWED — team draft, needs pharmacist/physician review

rules.label: Beta-blockers
rules.indications: Hypertension, coronary disease, arrhythmia, heart failure, migraine prophylaxis
rules.mechanism: Reduced cardiac output and skin blood flow; mask tachycardia
rules.clinician_note: Avoid midday outdoors; watch for unusual fatigue or dizziness
rules.patient_advice: This medicine lowers how hard your heart works, which makes it harder to cool down. Avoid being outside in the middle of the day, and watch for unusual tiredness or dizziness. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)
rules.reviewed_by: UNREVIEWED — team draft, needs pharmacist/physician review

rules.label: Lithium
rules.mechanism: Narrow therapeutic index; dehydration → reduced clearance → toxicity
rules.clinician_note: Monitor lithium levels; maintain hydration; do not stop on your own
rules.patient_advice: If you get dehydrated in the heat, the level of this medicine in your blood can rise too high. Keep drinking water. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)
rules.reviewed_by: UNREVIEWED — team draft, needs pharmacist/physician review

rules.label: Topiramate
rules.mechanism: Oligohidrosis/anhidrosis (notable in children; FDA label warning)
rules.clinician_note: Watch heat dissipation; children are the priority
rules.patient_advice: This medicine can reduce sweating, so your body cools down less well. Stay somewhere cool on hot days. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)

rules.label: Stimulants
rules.clinician_note: Avoid strenuous activity on hot days
rules.patient_advice: This medicine makes your body produce more heat. Avoid hard exercise on hot days. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)

rules.label: SSRIs / SNRIs
rules.patient_advice: In hot weather this medicine can lower the salt level in your blood. Watch for feeling very tired or confused. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.

rules.label: ACE inhibitors / ARBs
rules.mechanism: Reduced renal perfusion when dehydrated; AKI/hyperkalemia risk
rules.clinician_note: Watch for low urine output if vomiting/diarrhea during a heat wave
rules.patient_advice: If you get dehydrated, this medicine can put strain on your kidneys. Tell your doctor if you are passing much less urine, or if you have vomiting or diarrhoea. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
rules.source: Team drug-heat knowledge base v0.1 (Drug-Heat Risk Table.xlsx, 2026-09-19)

rules.label: SGLT2 inhibitors
rules.mechanism: Osmotic diuresis → volume depletion; eDKA risk
rules.clinician_note: Follow sick-day rules; ask the doctor about pausing
rules.patient_advice: This medicine makes you pass more water, so you can get dehydrated in the heat. Ask your doctor what to do on sick days. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.

rules.patient_advice: This medicine can make you less aware that you are thirsty. Drink water regularly on hot days. Never stop or change this medicine on your own — talk to your doctor first.
